phase: 15.3 — packed seed store vs the one-file-per-node reference store
measured_commit_subject: phase15.6: opt-in adaptive promotion of reusable intermediates
corpus: real100-v1 SUBSET: one document per (format, size_class) stratum = 12 documents (NOT the frozen 100-document population)
what_is_measured: the SAME descriptor is ingested twice into two independent store roots — `$d/fs` (one file per seed node) and `$d/pack --packed` (append-only fieldpack segments + an immutable per-segment index) — then persistent bytes, file count, cold-observation wall, and byte-exact materialization are compared

syscall_totals_one_cold_observation_stra.note: a single observation on a small document is ~parity (the packed index adds one pread); the structural win is file count and bytes, not per-call syscalls

interpretation: The packed seed store is a structural win that leaves semantics untouched: identical node identities and byte-exact reconstruction, 111x fewer files, 28% fewer persistent bytes, and parity cold-observation latency. It is the storage-substrate half of the Phase-15 thesis; it does not by itself reduce CPU.
limits_and_non_claims: subset of 12 documents, selected for format/size-class spread, not the full population
packed is a SEED-namespace backend only: descriptor/manifest/index/cache stay files, so the seek-based partial lane and FieldId are unchanged
no claim that packed is universally better; latency parity is the honest reading
the `perf` counter is unavailable in doc-baseline; strace + du/find are used instead
note_fixed_during_sealing: an earlier run of this court recorded `bin` = the debug path while building release, because BIN resolution consulted the doc-baseline `VOLE_BIN` env var; the script now ignores VOLE_BIN under PROFILE=release (mirroring the 15.1 real100-court fix) and this sealed run measured target/release/vole-document
tuning: none; the subset is chosen from pre-registered format/size strata, not from any measurement
